title: Annotations: the language ones, the framework ones and your own

videos.script: You have written @Override since lesson 24. This lesson is about what that @ is. {{label}} An annotation is a label on a declaration, and by itself it does nothing. Something has to read it. {{compiler}} First, the labels the compiler reads. A method that claims to override and does not. A method on its way out, and the warning every caller gets. {{retention}} Then the labels a framework reads. Some annotations vanish after compiling, some reach the class file, and some reach the running program. {{runner}} Only the last kind matters to a framework, and twenty lines of reflection show why. They find every method marked Check and run it. That is most of what a test framework does. {{own}} Last, an annotation of your own. A field that must not be blank, and the validator that gives the label its meaning. By the end, an annotation in somebody else's code tells you to look for whatever reads it.
